chest_pain_with_cardiopulmonary_features.title: Chest Pain with Cardiopulmonary Features
chest_pain_with_cardiopulmonary_features.body: Your symptoms include chest pressure combined with shortness of breath. This combination can indicate a serious cardiac or pulmonary condition that requires immediate medical evaluation. These symptoms together increase the concern for conditions like acute coronary syndrome or pulmonary embolism.

possible_cardiac_injury.title: Possible Cardiac Injury Detected
possible_cardiac_injury.body: Your troponin level, combined with your symptoms, suggests possible damage to heart muscle. Troponin is a protein released when heart cells are injured. Elevated levels require immediate medical evaluation to determine the cause and appropriate treatment.

troponin_description.title: About Troponin
troponin_description.body: Troponin is a protein found in heart muscle cells. When the heart is damaged, troponin is released into the bloodstream. Measuring troponin levels helps doctors detect heart injury, including heart attacks.

troponin_normal.title: Normal Troponin Level
troponin_normal.body: Your troponin level is within the normal reference range. This suggests no current evidence of heart muscle injury based on this test alone. However, if you are experiencing symptoms, continue to follow medical advice.

troponin_high.title: Elevated Troponin Level
troponin_high.body: Your troponin level is above the normal reference range. This may indicate some degree of heart muscle stress or injury. Further evaluation is recommended to determine the cause.

troponin_critical_high.title: Critically Elevated Troponin
troponin_critical_high.body: Your troponin level is significantly elevated, which strongly suggests heart muscle injury. This requires immediate medical evaluation. Do not delay seeking care.

cardiac_arrest_explanation.title: Signs of Cardiac Arrest
cardiac_arrest_explanation.body: The symptoms described indicate a possible cardiac arrest or life-threatening cardiac emergency. Immediate emergency response is critical. Call 911 immediately and begin CPR if the person is unresponsive and not breathing normally.

stroke_explanation.title: Signs of Stroke
stroke_explanation.body: The symptoms described may indicate a stroke. Time is critical in stroke treatment - every minute matters. Call 911 immediately. Remember FAST: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call 911.

severe_breathing_difficulty_explanation.title: Severe Breathing Difficulty
severe_breathing_difficulty_explanation.body: Severe difficulty breathing is a medical emergency. This can indicate serious conditions affecting the heart, lungs, or airways. Immediate emergency care is needed.

anaphylaxis_explanation.title: Signs of Severe Allergic Reaction
anaphylaxis_explanation.body: The symptoms described suggest anaphylaxis, a severe and potentially life-threatening allergic reaction. This requires immediate emergency treatment with epinephrine. Call 911 immediately.

uncontrolled_bleeding_explanation.title: Uncontrolled Bleeding
uncontrolled_bleeding_explanation.body: Severe, uncontrolled bleeding is a medical emergency. Apply direct pressure to the wound and call 911 immediately. Significant blood loss can be life-threatening.

loss_of_consciousness_explanation.title: Loss of Consciousness
loss_of_consciousness_explanation.body: Sudden loss of consciousness requires immediate emergency evaluation. This can indicate serious conditions affecting the heart, brain, or other vital organs.

diabetes_cardiac_risk_explanation.title: Diabetes Increases Cardiac Risk
diabetes_cardiac_risk_explanation.body: Diabetes is a significant risk factor for heart disease. Symptoms that might be less concerning in others warrant more urgent evaluation in people with diabetes.

troponin_with_symptoms_explanation.title: Elevated Troponin with Symptoms
troponin_with_symptoms_explanation.body: The combination of elevated troponin and your current symptoms is concerning for a cardiac event. This requires immediate emergency evaluation.

sob_severe_explanation.title: Severe Respiratory Distress
sob_severe_explanation.body: Your symptoms indicate severe difficulty breathing. This is a medical emergency that requires immediate attention. Severe respiratory distress can rapidly become life-threatening.

sob_chest_pain_explanation.title: Shortness of Breath with Chest Pain
sob_chest_pain_explanation.body: The combination of shortness of breath and chest pain requires urgent evaluation. This can indicate serious cardiac or pulmonary conditions including heart attack or pulmonary embolism.

sob_sudden_explanation.title: Sudden Onset Breathing Difficulty
sob_sudden_explanation.body: Sudden difficulty breathing that occurs at rest is concerning and requires prompt evaluation. This can indicate conditions like blood clots in the lungs, heart problems, or asthma attacks.

sob_fever_explanation.title: Breathing Difficulty with Fever
sob_fever_explanation.body: Shortness of breath combined with fever suggests a possible respiratory infection such as pneumonia. Medical evaluation is recommended to determine if treatment is needed.

sob_mild_explanation.title: Mild Exertional Shortness of Breath
sob_mild_explanation.body: Shortness of breath with activity but not at rest is common and often due to deconditioning, but should be evaluated to rule out underlying heart or lung conditions.

abd_emergency_explanation.title: Abdominal Emergency Signs
abd_emergency_explanation.body: Your symptoms suggest a possible surgical emergency. A rigid abdomen, vomiting blood, or blood in stool can indicate serious conditions requiring immediate surgery. Do not delay seeking care.

abd_severe_explanation.title: Severe Sudden Abdominal Pain
abd_severe_explanation.body: Sudden, severe abdominal pain requires urgent evaluation. This can indicate conditions like appendicitis, ruptured organ, or bowel obstruction that may need emergency treatment.

abd_appendicitis_explanation.title: Possible Appendicitis
abd_appendicitis_explanation.body: Pain in the right lower abdomen with fever is concerning for appendicitis. This condition requires medical evaluation and often surgical treatment if confirmed.

abd_gallbladder_explanation.title: Possible Gallbladder Issue
abd_gallbladder_explanation.body: Right upper abdominal pain with nausea may indicate gallbladder problems such as gallstones. Medical evaluation can confirm the diagnosis and determine appropriate treatment.

abd_mild_explanation.title: Mild Gastrointestinal Symptoms
abd_mild_explanation.body: Your symptoms suggest a mild gastrointestinal issue that should be monitored. Follow up with your doctor if symptoms persist or worsen.

ha_thunderclap_explanation.title: Thunderclap Headache Warning
ha_thunderclap_explanation.body: A sudden, severe headache reaching maximum intensity within seconds (thunderclap headache) can indicate bleeding in the brain. This is a medical emergency requiring immediate evaluation.

ha_meningitis_explanation.title: Possible Meningitis
ha_meningitis_explanation.body: Headache with stiff neck and fever can indicate meningitis, an infection of the membranes around the brain. This requires urgent medical evaluation and treatment.

ha_neuro_explanation.title: Headache with Neurological Symptoms
ha_neuro_explanation.body: Headache accompanied by confusion, weakness, or vision changes requires urgent evaluation. These symptoms can indicate serious conditions affecting the brain.

ha_trauma_explanation.title: Post-Traumatic Headache
ha_trauma_explanation.body: Headache following a head injury should be evaluated to rule out concussion or more serious brain injury. Watch for worsening symptoms.

ha_migraine_explanation.title: Migraine-Like Headache
ha_migraine_explanation.body: Your headache symptoms are consistent with migraine. While not immediately dangerous, you should follow up with your doctor for proper diagnosis and treatment options.

diz_stroke_explanation.title: Dizziness with Stroke Signs
diz_stroke_explanation.body: Dizziness combined with slurred speech or one-sided weakness can indicate a stroke. Time is critical - call 911 immediately. Remember FAST: Face, Arms, Speech, Time.

diz_cardiac_explanation.title: Dizziness with Cardiac Symptoms
diz_cardiac_explanation.body: Dizziness combined with chest pain or shortness of breath may indicate a heart problem. Urgent evaluation is needed to rule out cardiac causes.

diz_syncope_explanation.title: Fainting Episode
diz_syncope_explanation.body: Fainting (syncope) requires medical evaluation to determine the cause. Fainting can be caused by heart rhythm problems, low blood pressure, or neurological conditions.

diz_vertigo_explanation.title: Vertigo with Hearing Changes
diz_vertigo_explanation.body: Room-spinning dizziness with hearing loss or ringing in the ears may indicate an inner ear condition such as Meniere's disease. Medical evaluation is recommended.

diz_positional_explanation.title: Positional Vertigo
diz_positional_explanation.body: Dizziness triggered by position changes is often benign positional vertigo (BPPV). This is treatable and your doctor can perform specific maneuvers to help.

fever_meningitis_explanation.title: Fever with Meningitis Signs
fever_meningitis_explanation.body: High fever with stiff neck is a warning sign for meningitis, a serious infection requiring immediate treatment. Do not delay seeking emergency care.

fever_sepsis_explanation.title: Possible Sepsis
fever_sepsis_explanation.body: Fever with confusion or altered mental status can indicate sepsis, a life-threatening response to infection. Immediate medical treatment is critical.

fever_immuno_explanation.title: Fever in Immunocompromised Patient
fever_immuno_explanation.body: Fever in people with weakened immune systems requires urgent evaluation. Your body may not be able to fight infection normally, making prompt treatment essential.

fever_rash_explanation.title: Fever with Rash
fever_rash_explanation.body: Fever accompanied by rash should be evaluated promptly. While many causes are not serious, some rashes with fever indicate conditions requiring treatment.

fever_viral_explanation.title: Likely Viral Illness
fever_viral_explanation.body: Your symptoms suggest a viral infection. Most viral illnesses resolve on their own with rest and fluids. Monitor symptoms and follow up if not improving.

back_cauda_explanation.title: Cauda Equina Syndrome Warning
back_cauda_explanation.body: Back pain with leg weakness or bowel/bladder changes can indicate cauda equina syndrome, compression of nerves at the base of the spine. This requires emergency evaluation to prevent permanent damage.

back_infection_explanation.title: Possible Spinal Infection
back_infection_explanation.body: Severe back pain with fever may indicate a spinal infection. Prompt evaluation and treatment are needed to prevent serious complications.

back_trauma_explanation.title: Post-Traumatic Back Pain
back_trauma_explanation.body: Severe back pain following injury should be evaluated to rule out fracture or other serious injury. Avoid moving if you suspect spinal injury.

back_radiculopathy_explanation.title: Nerve Compression Symptoms
back_radiculopathy_explanation.body: Back pain radiating to the leg or causing numbness suggests nerve compression, often from a herniated disc. Medical evaluation can determine the best treatment approach.

back_mechanical_explanation.title: Mechanical Back Pain
back_mechanical_explanation.body: Your symptoms suggest common mechanical back pain from muscles or joints. Rest, over-the-counter pain relief, and gentle stretching often help. See your doctor if not improving.

nv_bleed_explanation.title: Vomiting Blood
nv_bleed_explanation.body: Vomiting blood is a medical emergency indicating bleeding in the upper digestive tract. Call 911 immediately. This requires urgent evaluation and treatment.

nv_meningitis_explanation.title: Vomiting with Meningitis Signs
nv_meningitis_explanation.body: Vomiting with headache and stiff neck can indicate meningitis. This serious infection requires immediate medical evaluation and treatment.

nv_dehydration_explanation.title: Dehydration Risk
nv_dehydration_explanation.body: Inability to keep fluids down or signs of dehydration require medical attention. Severe dehydration can affect organ function and may need IV fluid replacement.

nv_head_injury_explanation.title: Vomiting After Head Injury
nv_head_injury_explanation.body: Vomiting following a head injury can indicate a concussion or more serious brain injury. Medical evaluation is recommended.

nv_viral_explanation.title: Viral Gastroenteritis
nv_viral_explanation.body: Your symptoms suggest a viral stomach bug. Focus on staying hydrated with small, frequent sips of clear fluids. Most cases resolve within a few days.

fatigue_stroke_explanation.title: Weakness with Stroke Signs
fatigue_stroke_explanation.body: Sudden weakness on one side of the body with speech difficulties indicates a possible stroke. Call 911 immediately - time is critical for stroke treatment.

fatigue_cardiac_explanation.title: Fatigue with Cardiac Symptoms
fatigue_cardiac_explanation.body: Fatigue combined with chest pain or shortness of breath requires urgent cardiac evaluation. These symptoms can indicate heart problems.

fatigue_infection_explanation.title: Fatigue with Fever
fatigue_infection_explanation.body: Fatigue accompanied by fever suggests your body is fighting an infection. Medical evaluation can determine if treatment is needed.

fatigue_weight_loss_explanation.title: Fatigue with Unexplained Weight Loss
fatigue_weight_loss_explanation.body: Persistent fatigue with unintentional weight loss warrants medical evaluation to rule out underlying conditions that may need treatment.

fatigue_chronic_explanation.title: Chronic Fatigue
fatigue_chronic_explanation.body: Persistent fatigue lasting several weeks should be evaluated. Many conditions can cause prolonged fatigue, and proper diagnosis leads to appropriate treatment.

cough_blood_explanation.title: Coughing Up Blood
cough_blood_explanation.body: Coughing up blood (hemoptysis) requires urgent medical evaluation. While sometimes caused by minor issues, it can indicate serious lung conditions.

cough_distress_explanation.title: Severe Cough with Respiratory Distress
cough_distress_explanation.body: Cough with significant shortness of breath and wheezing indicates respiratory distress requiring urgent evaluation. This may indicate asthma, COPD exacerbation, or other serious conditions.

cough_pneumonia_explanation.title: Possible Pneumonia
cough_pneumonia_explanation.body: Cough with fever and chest pain suggests possible pneumonia. Medical evaluation is needed to confirm diagnosis and determine if antibiotics are necessary.

cough_chronic_explanation.title: Chronic Cough
cough_chronic_explanation.body: A cough lasting several weeks with night sweats should be evaluated. Various conditions can cause chronic cough and proper diagnosis guides treatment.

cough_viral_explanation.title: Viral Upper Respiratory Infection
cough_viral_explanation.body: Your cough with sore throat suggests a viral infection. Rest, fluids, and symptom relief are the main treatments. See your doctor if not improving after 7-10 days.

throat_airway_explanation.title: Airway Compromise Warning
throat_airway_explanation.body: Difficulty breathing or drooling with sore throat suggests possible airway obstruction. This is a medical emergency - call 911 immediately.

throat_abscess_explanation.title: Possible Peritonsillar Abscess
throat_abscess_explanation.body: Severe sore throat with difficulty swallowing and muffled voice may indicate a peritonsillar abscess. This infection requires urgent medical treatment.

throat_strep_explanation.title: Possible Strep Throat
throat_strep_explanation.body: Sore throat with fever and swollen lymph nodes may be strep throat. A quick test can confirm, and antibiotics are needed if positive to prevent complications.

throat_scarlet_explanation.title: Sore Throat with Rash
throat_scarlet_explanation.body: Fever with sore throat and rash can indicate scarlet fever or other conditions requiring evaluation and treatment.

throat_viral_explanation.title: Viral Pharyngitis
throat_viral_explanation.body: Your sore throat with cough suggests a viral infection. Rest and symptom relief are the main treatments. Most viral sore throats improve within a week.

uri_retention_explanation.title: Urinary Retention
uri_retention_explanation.body: Inability to urinate is a medical emergency. The bladder must be drained to prevent damage. Seek immediate medical care.

uri_kidney_explanation.title: Possible Kidney Infection
uri_kidney_explanation.body: Fever with flank pain suggests a kidney infection (pyelonephritis). This requires prompt antibiotic treatment to prevent serious complications.

uri_stone_explanation.title: Possible Kidney Stone
uri_stone_explanation.body: Severe flank pain with blood in urine is typical of a kidney stone. Medical evaluation can confirm diagnosis and provide pain management.

uri_uti_fever_explanation.title: UTI with Fever
uri_uti_fever_explanation.body: Urinary symptoms with fever may indicate the infection has spread beyond the bladder. Prompt medical evaluation and treatment are needed.

uri_simple_explanation.title: Simple Urinary Tract Infection
uri_simple_explanation.body: Your symptoms suggest a bladder infection. Antibiotics are typically needed for treatment. Drink plenty of fluids and see your doctor.

rash_anaphylaxis_explanation.title: Rash with Anaphylaxis Signs
rash_anaphylaxis_explanation.body: Rash with breathing difficulty or throat/face swelling indicates anaphylaxis. This is a life-threatening emergency. Use an EpiPen if available and call 911.

rash_meningococcal_explanation.title: Concerning Rash with Fever
rash_meningococcal_explanation.body: Fever with a petechial rash (tiny non-blanching spots) can indicate meningococcal disease. This is a medical emergency requiring immediate treatment.

rash_severe_explanation.title: Severe Skin Reaction
rash_severe_explanation.body: Painful or blistering rash requires urgent evaluation. Some skin reactions can be serious and need prompt medical treatment.

rash_spreading_explanation.title: Spreading Rash with Fever
rash_spreading_explanation.body: A rapidly spreading rash with fever should be evaluated promptly. This can indicate infections or conditions requiring treatment.

rash_mild_explanation.title: Mild Rash
rash_mild_explanation.body: Your rash without fever or systemic symptoms is likely not urgent. However, follow up with your doctor for proper diagnosis and treatment if it persists.

joint_septic_explanation.title: Possible Septic Joint
joint_septic_explanation.body: A hot, swollen joint with fever may indicate a joint infection. This is a medical emergency that can cause permanent joint damage if not treated promptly.

joint_fracture_explanation.title: Possible Fracture
joint_fracture_explanation.body: Inability to bear weight after injury suggests possible fracture. X-rays are needed to evaluate and determine appropriate treatment.

joint_gout_explanation.title: Acute Joint Inflammation
joint_gout_explanation.body: A red, swollen, painful joint may indicate gout or another inflammatory condition. Medical evaluation can confirm diagnosis and provide treatment.

joint_inflammatory_explanation.title: Inflammatory Arthritis Pattern
joint_inflammatory_explanation.body: Multiple joint pain with morning stiffness suggests an inflammatory arthritis. Your doctor can evaluate and discuss treatment options.

joint_mechanical_explanation.title: Mechanical Joint Pain
joint_mechanical_explanation.body: Your joint pain without signs of infection or inflammation is likely mechanical. Rest, over-the-counter pain relief, and gentle exercise often help.

anx_suicidal_explanation.title: Crisis Support Needed
anx_suicidal_explanation.body: Thoughts of suicide or self-harm require immediate support. You are not alone. Call 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) or go to your nearest emergency room. Help is available.

anx_cardiac_explanation.title: First-Time Chest Pain with Anxiety
anx_cardiac_explanation.body: First-time chest pain, even with anxiety, should be evaluated to rule out cardiac causes. Anxiety and heart conditions can have similar symptoms.

anx_first_panic_explanation.title: First Panic Attack
anx_first_panic_explanation.body: If this is your first panic attack, medical evaluation is recommended to rule out other conditions and discuss management strategies.

anx_panic_explanation.title: Panic Attack Symptoms
anx_panic_explanation.body: Your symptoms are consistent with a panic attack. While frightening, panic attacks are not dangerous. Follow up with your doctor to discuss treatment options.

anx_mild_explanation.title: Anxiety Symptoms
anx_mild_explanation.body: Your anxiety symptoms should be discussed with your doctor. Effective treatments are available including therapy and medication.

palp_syncope_explanation.title: Palpitations with Fainting
palp_syncope_explanation.body: Palpitations that cause fainting can indicate a serious heart rhythm problem. This is an emergency requiring immediate evaluation.

palp_cardiac_explanation.title: Palpitations with Cardiac Symptoms
palp_cardiac_explanation.body: Palpitations with chest pain or shortness of breath need urgent evaluation to rule out dangerous heart rhythm problems.

palp_prolonged_explanation.title: Prolonged Palpitation Episode
palp_prolonged_explanation.body: A prolonged episode of racing heart at rest should be evaluated. Some arrhythmias need medical intervention to convert to normal rhythm.

palp_known_explanation.title: Palpitations in Heart Patient
palp_known_explanation.body: People with known heart conditions should have new or changing palpitations evaluated promptly to ensure appropriate management.

palp_benign_explanation.title: Likely Benign Palpitations
palp_benign_explanation.body: Palpitations triggered by caffeine or stimulants are often benign. Reducing caffeine may help. See your doctor if symptoms persist.

numb_stroke_explanation.title: Numbness with Stroke Signs
numb_stroke_explanation.body: Sudden numbness with face drooping, arm weakness, or speech difficulty indicates a possible stroke. Call 911 immediately - time is critical.

numb_sudden_explanation.title: Sudden One-Sided Numbness
numb_sudden_explanation.body: Sudden numbness affecting one side of the body is a stroke warning sign. Call 911 immediately for evaluation.

numb_spinal_explanation.title: Spinal Cord Compression Warning
numb_spinal_explanation.body: Numbness with back pain and bowel/bladder changes may indicate spinal cord compression. This requires urgent evaluation to prevent permanent damage.

numb_compression_explanation.title: Nerve Compression
numb_compression_explanation.body: Numbness after injury may indicate nerve compression. Medical evaluation can determine the cause and appropriate treatment.

numb_peripheral_explanation.title: Peripheral Neuropathy
numb_peripheral_explanation.body: Numbness in both hands and feet developing gradually suggests peripheral neuropathy. See your doctor to identify the cause and treatment options.

vis_sudden_explanation.title: Sudden Vision Loss
vis_sudden_explanation.body: Sudden vision loss is a medical emergency. This can indicate stroke, retinal artery blockage, or other conditions requiring immediate treatment to preserve vision.

vis_retinal_explanation.title: Possible Retinal Detachment
vis_retinal_explanation.body: Flashing lights with a curtain-like shadow in your vision suggests retinal detachment. This requires emergency eye evaluation to prevent permanent vision loss.

vis_glaucoma_explanation.title: Possible Acute Glaucoma
vis_glaucoma_explanation.body: Eye pain with headache and vision changes can indicate acute angle-closure glaucoma. This is an emergency requiring immediate treatment to preserve vision.

vis_diplopia_explanation.title: New Double Vision
vis_diplopia_explanation.body: New double vision should be evaluated promptly. It can indicate problems with eye muscles, nerves, or brain that require diagnosis.

vis_floaters_explanation.title: New Floaters
vis_floaters_explanation.body: New floaters without flashing lights should be evaluated by an eye doctor, though usually not urgently. They can sometimes indicate retinal problems.

ear_mastoid_explanation.title: Possible Mastoiditis
ear_mastoid_explanation.body: Swelling and pain behind the ear with fever can indicate mastoiditis, a serious infection of the bone behind the ear. Urgent treatment is needed.

ear_facial_explanation.title: Ear Infection with Facial Nerve Involvement
ear_facial_explanation.body: Facial weakness with ear infection suggests the infection may be affecting the facial nerve. Urgent evaluation and treatment are needed.

ear_severe_explanation.title: Severe Ear Infection
ear_severe_explanation.body: Severe ear pain with fever indicates a significant infection requiring medical evaluation and likely antibiotic treatment.

ear_swimmers_explanation.title: Swimmer's Ear
ear_swimmers_explanation.body: Ear pain after swimming with drainage suggests swimmer's ear (outer ear infection). Antibiotic ear drops are typically needed for treatment.

ear_mild_explanation.title: Mild Ear Infection
ear_mild_explanation.body: Ear pain with recent cold symptoms may indicate a mild middle ear infection. See your doctor to determine if antibiotics are needed.

allergy_anaphylaxis_explanation.title: Anaphylaxis
allergy_anaphylaxis_explanation.body: Breathing difficulty, throat swelling, or tongue swelling after allergen exposure indicates anaphylaxis. Use an EpiPen if available and call 911 immediately.

allergy_severe_explanation.title: Severe Allergic Reaction
allergy_severe_explanation.body: Facial swelling or dizziness during an allergic reaction indicates a severe response requiring emergency evaluation.

allergy_progressive_explanation.title: Progressive Allergic Reaction
allergy_progressive_explanation.body: Widespread hives with vomiting suggest the allergic reaction is progressing. Medical evaluation is needed to prevent worsening.

allergy_hives_explanation.title: Hives
allergy_hives_explanation.body: Hives (urticaria) without breathing symptoms are usually not dangerous but should be evaluated. Antihistamines may provide relief.

allergy_mild_explanation.title: Mild Allergic Reaction
allergy_mild_explanation.body: Mild allergic reactions without breathing symptoms can often be managed with antihistamines. See your doctor if symptoms persist or for future prevention.

leg_pe_explanation.title: Possible Pulmonary Embolism
leg_pe_explanation.body: Leg swelling with sudden shortness of breath or chest pain may indicate a blood clot has traveled to the lungs. This is a life-threatening emergency - call 911.

leg_dvt_explanation.title: High Risk for Blood Clot
leg_dvt_explanation.body: A swollen, painful, warm leg strongly suggests a deep vein thrombosis (blood clot). Urgent evaluation is needed to prevent the clot from traveling to the lungs.

leg_dvt_risk_explanation.title: DVT Risk with Risk Factors
leg_dvt_risk_explanation.body: Leg swelling after surgery or prolonged immobility increases blood clot risk. Medical evaluation is recommended.

leg_unilateral_explanation.title: One-Sided Leg Swelling
leg_unilateral_explanation.body: Sudden swelling in one leg should be evaluated for possible blood clot. Ultrasound can determine if a clot is present.

leg_bilateral_explanation.title: Both Legs Swollen
leg_bilateral_explanation.body: Swelling in both legs that develops gradually may indicate heart, kidney, or liver problems. See your doctor for evaluation.

glucose_description.title: About Blood Glucose
glucose_description.body: Blood glucose measures sugar in your blood. Your body uses glucose for energy. Levels that are too high or too low can cause symptoms and health problems.

glucose_critical_low.title: Dangerously Low Blood Sugar
glucose_critical_low.body: Your blood sugar is critically low. This requires immediate treatment with fast-acting sugar (juice, glucose tablets) and emergency care if you cannot treat yourself.

glucose_low.title: Low Blood Sugar
glucose_low.body: Your blood sugar is below normal. Eat or drink something with sugar and monitor your levels. See your doctor to discuss prevention.

glucose_normal.title: Normal Blood Glucose
glucose_normal.body: Your blood glucose is within the normal range, suggesting normal glucose metabolism at the time of testing.

glucose_high.title: Elevated Blood Sugar
glucose_high.body: Your blood sugar is above normal. This may indicate prediabetes or diabetes. Follow up with your doctor for further evaluation.

glucose_critical_high.title: Dangerously High Blood Sugar
glucose_critical_high.body: Your blood sugar is dangerously elevated. This can lead to serious complications and requires immediate medical attention.

hemoglobin_description.title: About Hemoglobin
hemoglobin_description.body: Hemoglobin is a protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen throughout your body. Low hemoglobin indicates anemia, while high levels may indicate other conditions.

hemoglobin_critical_low.title: Severely Low Hemoglobin
hemoglobin_critical_low.body: Your hemoglobin is critically low, indicating severe anemia. This may require blood transfusion and requires immediate medical evaluation.

hemoglobin_low.title: Low Hemoglobin
hemoglobin_low.body: Your hemoglobin is below normal, indicating anemia. Common causes include iron deficiency, blood loss, or chronic disease. Further testing is needed.

hemoglobin_normal.title: Normal Hemoglobin
hemoglobin_normal.body: Your hemoglobin is within the normal range, suggesting adequate oxygen-carrying capacity of your blood.

hemoglobin_high.title: Elevated Hemoglobin
hemoglobin_high.body: Your hemoglobin is above normal. This can occur with dehydration, smoking, or conditions causing overproduction of red blood cells.

hemoglobin_critical_high.title: Critically High Hemoglobin
hemoglobin_critical_high.body: Your hemoglobin is significantly elevated. This increases blood clot risk and requires evaluation.

hematocrit_description.title: About Hematocrit
hematocrit_description.body: Hematocrit measures the percentage of your blood that is red blood cells. It helps evaluate anemia and other blood conditions.

hematocrit_critical_low.title: Critically Low Hematocrit
hematocrit_critical_low.body: Your hematocrit is dangerously low, indicating severe anemia. Immediate medical evaluation is needed.

hematocrit_low.title: Low Hematocrit
hematocrit_low.body: Your hematocrit is below normal, suggesting anemia. Follow up with your doctor to determine the cause.

hematocrit_normal.title: Normal Hematocrit
hematocrit_normal.body: Your hematocrit is within normal range.

hematocrit_high.title: Elevated Hematocrit
hematocrit_high.body: Your hematocrit is above normal. This can indicate dehydration or conditions causing increased red blood cell production.

hematocrit_critical_high.title: Critically High Hematocrit
hematocrit_critical_high.body: Your hematocrit is significantly elevated, increasing blood clot risk. Medical evaluation is needed.

hematocrit_abnormal.title: Abnormal Hematocrit
hematocrit_abnormal.body: Your hematocrit is outside the normal range. Follow up with your doctor for further evaluation.

wbc_description.title: About White Blood Cell Count
wbc_description.body: White blood cells fight infection. High counts often indicate infection or inflammation, while low counts may indicate immune system problems.

wbc_critical_low.title: Severely Low White Blood Cells
wbc_critical_low.body: Your white blood cell count is dangerously low, making you vulnerable to infections. Avoid sick contacts and seek medical care for any fever.

wbc_low.title: Low White Blood Cells
wbc_low.body: Your white blood cell count is below normal. This can be caused by medications, infections, or bone marrow problems.

wbc_normal.title: Normal White Blood Cell Count
wbc_normal.body: Your white blood cell count is within the normal range.

wbc_high.title: Elevated White Blood Cells
wbc_high.body: Your white blood cell count is elevated, often indicating your body is fighting an infection or inflammation.

wbc_critical_high.title: Severely Elevated White Blood Cells
wbc_critical_high.body: Your white blood cell count is markedly elevated. This requires evaluation to determine the cause.

wbc_abnormal.title: Abnormal White Blood Cell Count
wbc_abnormal.body: Your white blood cell count is outside the normal range. Follow up with your doctor for evaluation.

platelet_description.title: About Platelet Count
platelet_description.body: Platelets help your blood clot. Low platelet counts increase bleeding risk, while high counts may increase clotting risk.

platelet_critical_low.title: Critically Low Platelets
platelet_critical_low.body: Your platelet count is dangerously low, increasing your risk of serious bleeding. Avoid activities that could cause injury and seek immediate medical care.

platelet_low.title: Low Platelets
platelet_low.body: Your platelet count is below normal. This may increase bruising and bleeding risk. Further evaluation is needed.

platelet_normal.title: Normal Platelet Count
platelet_normal.body: Your platelet count is within the normal range.

platelet_high.title: Elevated Platelets
platelet_high.body: Your platelet count is above normal. This can occur with infection, inflammation, or other conditions.

platelet_critical_high.title: Very High Platelets
platelet_critical_high.body: Your platelet count is significantly elevated. This may increase clotting risk and requires evaluation.

creatinine_description.title: About Creatinine
creatinine_description.body: Creatinine is a waste product filtered by your kidneys. High levels may indicate reduced kidney function.

creatinine_low.title: Low Creatinine
creatinine_low.body: Low creatinine is usually not concerning and may relate to low muscle mass or diet.

creatinine_normal.title: Normal Creatinine
creatinine_normal.body: Your creatinine level is normal, suggesting your kidneys are filtering properly.

creatinine_high.title: Elevated Creatinine
creatinine_high.body: Your creatinine is elevated, which may indicate reduced kidney function. Further evaluation is recommended.

creatinine_critical_high.title: Severely Elevated Creatinine
creatinine_critical_high.body: Your creatinine is severely elevated, indicating significant kidney dysfunction. Immediate medical evaluation is needed.

bun_description.title: About BUN
bun_description.body: Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) is a waste product filtered by your kidneys. Elevated levels can indicate kidney problems or dehydration.

bun_low.title: Low BUN
bun_low.body: Low BUN is usually not concerning and may indicate low protein intake or liver issues.

bun_normal.title: Normal BUN
bun_normal.body: Your BUN level is within the normal range.

bun_high.title: Elevated BUN
bun_high.body: Your BUN is elevated. This can indicate dehydration, kidney problems, or high protein intake.

bun_critical_high.title: Severely Elevated BUN
bun_critical_high.body: Your BUN is severely elevated, indicating significant kidney dysfunction or severe dehydration. Medical evaluation is needed.

sodium_description.title: About Sodium
sodium_description.body: Sodium is an electrolyte essential for nerve and muscle function. Both high and low levels can cause serious symptoms.

sodium_critical_low.title: Critically Low Sodium
sodium_critical_low.body: Your sodium is dangerously low. This can cause confusion, seizures, and requires immediate medical treatment.

sodium_low.title: Low Sodium
sodium_low.body: Your sodium is below normal. This may cause symptoms like nausea, headache, or confusion.

sodium_normal.title: Normal Sodium
sodium_normal.body: Your sodium level is within the normal range.

sodium_high.title: Elevated Sodium
sodium_high.body: Your sodium is above normal, often indicating dehydration. Increased fluid intake may help.

sodium_critical_high.title: Critically High Sodium
sodium_critical_high.body: Your sodium is dangerously elevated. This requires immediate medical treatment.

sodium_critical.title: Critical Sodium Level
sodium_critical.body: Your sodium level is critically abnormal and requires immediate medical attention.

sodium_abnormal.title: Abnormal Sodium
sodium_abnormal.body: Your sodium is outside the normal range. Follow up with your doctor for evaluation.

potassium_description.title: About Potassium
potassium_description.body: Potassium is essential for heart and muscle function. Both high and low levels can cause dangerous heart rhythm problems.

potassium_critical_low.title: Critically Low Potassium
potassium_critical_low.body: Your potassium is dangerously low. This can cause dangerous heart rhythms and requires immediate treatment.

potassium_low.title: Low Potassium
potassium_low.body: Your potassium is below normal. This may cause muscle weakness, cramps, or irregular heartbeat.

potassium_normal.title: Normal Potassium
potassium_normal.body: Your potassium level is within the normal range.

potassium_high.title: Elevated Potassium
potassium_high.body: Your potassium is above normal. High potassium can affect heart rhythm and should be monitored.

potassium_critical_high.title: Critically High Potassium
potassium_critical_high.body: Your potassium is dangerously elevated. This can cause life-threatening heart rhythm problems and requires immediate treatment.

potassium_critical.title: Critical Potassium Level
potassium_critical.body: Your potassium is at a critical level that can cause dangerous heart rhythm problems. Immediate medical attention is required.

potassium_abnormal.title: Abnormal Potassium
potassium_abnormal.body: Your potassium is outside the normal range and should be evaluated promptly.

chloride_description.title: About Chloride
chloride_description.body: Chloride is an electrolyte that helps maintain fluid balance and acid-base balance in your body.

chloride_critical_low.title: Critically Low Chloride
chloride_critical_low.body: Your chloride is critically low, which may indicate metabolic problems requiring medical evaluation.

chloride_low.title: Low Chloride
chloride_low.body: Your chloride is below normal. This is often associated with other electrolyte imbalances.

chloride_normal.title: Normal Chloride
chloride_normal.body: Your chloride level is within the normal range.

chloride_high.title: Elevated Chloride
chloride_high.body: Your chloride is above normal. This may indicate dehydration or acid-base imbalance.

chloride_critical_high.title: Critically High Chloride
chloride_critical_high.body: Your chloride is critically elevated, requiring medical evaluation.

chloride_critical.title: Critical Chloride Level
chloride_critical.body: Your chloride level is critically abnormal and requires evaluation.

chloride_abnormal.title: Abnormal Chloride
chloride_abnormal.body: Your chloride is outside the normal range. Follow up with your doctor.

co2_description.title: About CO2/Bicarbonate
co2_description.body: CO2 (bicarbonate) reflects your body's acid-base balance. Abnormal levels can indicate kidney, lung, or metabolic problems.

co2_critical_low.title: Critically Low CO2
co2_critical_low.body: Your CO2 is critically low, indicating severe metabolic acidosis. This requires immediate medical attention.

co2_low.title: Low CO2
co2_low.body: Your CO2 is below normal, which may indicate mild acidosis or rapid breathing.

co2_normal.title: Normal CO2
co2_normal.body: Your CO2 level is within the normal range.

co2_high.title: Elevated CO2
co2_high.body: Your CO2 is above normal, which may indicate metabolic alkalosis or compensation for respiratory issues.

co2_critical_high.title: Critically High CO2
co2_critical_high.body: Your CO2 is critically elevated, requiring medical evaluation.

co2_abnormal.title: Abnormal CO2
co2_abnormal.body: Your CO2 is outside the normal range. Follow up with your doctor.

calcium_description.title: About Calcium
calcium_description.body: Calcium is essential for bones, muscles, nerves, and heart function. Both high and low levels can cause significant symptoms.

calcium_critical_low.title: Critically Low Calcium
calcium_critical_low.body: Your calcium is dangerously low. This can cause muscle spasms, numbness, and irregular heartbeat. Immediate treatment is needed.

calcium_low.title: Low Calcium
calcium_low.body: Your calcium is below normal. This may cause muscle cramps, numbness, or fatigue.

calcium_normal.title: Normal Calcium
calcium_normal.body: Your calcium level is within the normal range.

calcium_high.title: Elevated Calcium
calcium_high.body: Your calcium is above normal. This may cause fatigue, constipation, or confusion.

calcium_critical_high.title: Critically High Calcium
calcium_critical_high.body: Your calcium is dangerously elevated. This can affect heart rhythm and kidney function. Immediate medical attention is needed.

calcium_abnormal.title: Abnormal Calcium
calcium_abnormal.body: Your calcium is outside the normal range. Follow up with your doctor.

magnesium_description.title: About Magnesium
magnesium_description.body: Magnesium is essential for muscle, nerve, and heart function. Both high and low levels can cause significant symptoms.

magnesium_critical_low.title: Critically Low Magnesium
magnesium_critical_low.body: Your magnesium is dangerously low. This can cause muscle spasms, irregular heartbeat, and seizures.

magnesium_low.title: Low Magnesium
magnesium_low.body: Your magnesium is below normal. This may cause muscle cramps, fatigue, or irregular heartbeat.

magnesium_normal.title: Normal Magnesium
magnesium_normal.body: Your magnesium level is within the normal range.

magnesium_high.title: Elevated Magnesium
magnesium_high.body: Your magnesium is above normal. High magnesium can cause weakness or slow heart rate.

magnesium_critical_high.title: Critically High Magnesium
magnesium_critical_high.body: Your magnesium is dangerously elevated. This can cause dangerous heart rhythm problems.

magnesium_critical.title: Critical Magnesium Level
magnesium_critical.body: Your magnesium is at a critical level requiring medical attention.

magnesium_abnormal.title: Abnormal Magnesium
magnesium_abnormal.body: Your magnesium is outside the normal range. Follow up with your doctor.

ast_description.title: About AST
ast_description.body: AST (SGOT) is an enzyme found in the liver and other tissues. Elevated levels may indicate liver damage, but can also come from heart or muscle injury.

ast_normal.title: Normal AST
ast_normal.body: Your AST level is within the normal range.

ast_high.title: Elevated AST
ast_high.body: Your AST is above normal, which may indicate liver stress or injury. Further evaluation is recommended.

ast_critical_high.title: Severely Elevated AST
ast_critical_high.body: Your AST is markedly elevated, indicating significant liver or tissue injury. Urgent medical evaluation is needed.

alt_description.title: About ALT
alt_description.body: ALT (SGPT) is a liver enzyme. Elevated levels are more specific to liver damage than AST.

alt_normal.title: Normal ALT
alt_normal.body: Your ALT level is within the normal range.

alt_high.title: Elevated ALT
alt_high.body: Your ALT is above normal, suggesting possible liver inflammation or injury. Further evaluation is recommended.

alt_critical_high.title: Severely Elevated ALT
alt_critical_high.body: Your ALT is markedly elevated, indicating significant liver injury. Urgent medical evaluation is needed.

bilirubin_description.title: About Bilirubin
bilirubin_description.body: Bilirubin is a yellow pigment processed by the liver. High levels can cause yellowing of the skin (jaundice) and indicate liver or bile duct problems.

bilirubin_normal.title: Normal Bilirubin
bilirubin_normal.body: Your bilirubin level is within the normal range.

bilirubin_high.title: Elevated Bilirubin
bilirubin_high.body: Your bilirubin is elevated. This may cause yellowing of the skin or eyes and warrants evaluation.

bilirubin_critical_high.title: Severely Elevated Bilirubin
bilirubin_critical_high.body: Your bilirubin is markedly elevated, indicating significant liver or bile duct problems. Urgent evaluation is needed.

alkaline_phosphatase_description.title: About Alkaline Phosphatase
alkaline_phosphatase_description.body: Alkaline phosphatase is an enzyme found in liver, bone, and other tissues. Elevated levels may indicate liver, bone, or bile duct problems.

alk_phos_low.title: Low Alkaline Phosphatase
alk_phos_low.body: Low alkaline phosphatase is uncommon and may indicate nutritional deficiencies.

alk_phos_normal.title: Normal Alkaline Phosphatase
alk_phos_normal.body: Your alkaline phosphatase level is within the normal range.

alk_phos_high.title: Elevated Alkaline Phosphatase
alk_phos_high.body: Your alkaline phosphatase is elevated. This may indicate liver or bone conditions.

alk_phos_critical_high.title: Markedly Elevated Alkaline Phosphatase
alk_phos_critical_high.body: Your alkaline phosphatase is markedly elevated, which may indicate bile duct obstruction or bone disease.

tsh_description.title: About TSH
tsh_description.body: TSH (thyroid stimulating hormone) reflects thyroid function. High TSH suggests underactive thyroid, while low TSH suggests overactive thyroid.

tsh_critical_low.title: Critically Low TSH
tsh_critical_low.body: Your TSH is very low, indicating possible hyperthyroidism (overactive thyroid). This can cause rapid heart rate, anxiety, and weight loss.

tsh_low.title: Low TSH
tsh_low.body: Your TSH is below normal, suggesting possible overactive thyroid. Follow up with your doctor.

tsh_normal.title: Normal TSH
tsh_normal.body: Your TSH level is within the normal range, suggesting normal thyroid function.

tsh_high.title: Elevated TSH
tsh_high.body: Your TSH is elevated, suggesting possible underactive thyroid. This can cause fatigue, weight gain, and cold intolerance.

tsh_critical_high.title: Severely Elevated TSH
tsh_critical_high.body: Your TSH is markedly elevated, indicating significant hypothyroidism that requires treatment.

tsh_abnormal.title: Abnormal TSH
tsh_abnormal.body: Your TSH is outside the normal range. Follow up with your doctor for thyroid evaluation.

hba1c_description.title: About Hemoglobin A1c
hba1c_description.body: HbA1c reflects your average blood sugar over the past 2-3 months. It's used to diagnose and monitor diabetes.

hba1c_normal.title: Normal HbA1c
hba1c_normal.body: Your HbA1c is in the normal range, suggesting good blood sugar control over recent months.

hba1c_high.title: Elevated HbA1c
hba1c_high.body: Your HbA1c is elevated, indicating higher than normal average blood sugar. This may indicate prediabetes or diabetes.

hba1c_critical_high.title: Very High HbA1c
hba1c_critical_high.body: Your HbA1c is significantly elevated, indicating poorly controlled diabetes. This increases risk of complications and requires medical attention.

d_dimer_description.title: About D-Dimer
d_dimer_description.body: D-dimer is a protein fragment produced when blood clots dissolve. Elevated levels may indicate abnormal clotting activity.

d_dimer_normal.title: Normal D-Dimer
d_dimer_normal.body: Your D-dimer is within the normal range. A normal result helps rule out active blood clots.

d_dimer_high.title: Elevated D-Dimer
d_dimer_high.body: Your D-dimer is elevated. While this doesn't confirm a blood clot, it may warrant further testing to rule out DVT or pulmonary embolism.

d_dimer_critical_high.title: Markedly Elevated D-Dimer
d_dimer_critical_high.body: Your D-dimer is significantly elevated. Combined with your symptoms, this raises concern for blood clots and requires evaluation.
